subject: design/code-gate-mirror
statement: The blocking gate is for **correctness** — properties that are pure functions of the code (DINV-2). A **measurement** (how fast, how big, how expensive) is a different kind of thing: it depends on the environment, so it is *recorded and trended*, never asserted as a build-failing pass/fail (DINV-3). The #600 strand was precisely a measurement — a wall-clock budget over a git-history-derived diff — welded onto the correctness runner and failing when the machine changed; the offending check's own comment conceded the valid latency claim "is a Phase-B measure across real dogfood runs" while asserting a single-run budget anyway.
